questions.question: Which statement is NOT true according to the passage?

options.text: The tomb was unusually small for a pharaoh's burial.
Howard Carter's team discovered the tomb's entranceway on November 26, 1922.
The tomb appears to have been finished quickly as the paint wasn't dry when it was sealed.
Tutankhamun's tomb was lavishly filled with gold artifacts.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

If you read the last part, you will find, **"*Howard Carter's team discovered the tomb's entranceway on November 4, 1922*"**. This tells that the statement in option 2 is incorrect.

Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Tutankhamun had a short rule. Most of his time was used in:

looking after the well- being of his people

questions.question: Tutankhamun's father was a revolutionary. What was his revolution?

options.text: Images and names of all the Egyptians deities had to be destroyed.
He wanted his people to be polytheistic.
He wanted the Egyptians to worship one God - Aten.
Egyptians were asked to have no religion and no god.

questions.solution:

It is mentioned in the passage that ***"a revolutionary pharaoh who tried to focus Egypt's polytheistic religion around the worship of the sun disc, the Aten." ** *This sentence gives the answer to the question.

Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The discovery of a number of canes in the tomb indicates that Tutankhamun:

questions.question: What is the main theme of the passage?

options.text: The death of Tutankhamun and his burial
The life and death of the boy Pharaoh
The discovery of an incredible treasure

After reading the passage, you will find that it revolves around the boy Pharaoh. questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word**

ENTHUSIASM
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3) i.e. "Apathy".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ENTHUSIASM (उत्साह) **- Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.

 
 
• **Example**: His enthusiasm for the project was contagious.
 
 
 
• **Apathy (उदासीनता)** - Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.
 
 
• **Example**: The widespread apathy among students was concerning.
 
 
 
• The word "**Apathy**" is an antonym of "**ENTHUSIASM**" because it describes a state of indifference or lack of enthusiasm, directly opposing the concept of keen interest and spirited enjoyment implied by enthusiasm.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Apathy".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fervor (उत्साह)** - Intense and passionate feeling.

 
 
• **Example**: She spoke with fervor about her beliefs.
 
 
 
• **Zeal (जोश)** - Great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective.
 
 
• **Example**: He approached the project with zeal.
 
 
 
• **Nervousness (घबराहट) **- The state of being anxious or apprehensive.
 
 
• **Example**: Her nervousness was evident before the performance.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

The assistant in the library picked up the books from the tables and put ______ back on the shelves.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **them**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context tells us that the library assistant removed the **books** from the tables and rearranged** them** on the bookshelves.
 
• The sentence requires a **plural** **pronoun **which refers to the 'books' (plural).
 
• As 'its' is a **singular possessive pronoun**, it is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• 'they' is a **subjective pronoun** and 'it' is a **singular pronoun** and hence, they are the incorrect options.
 
• **Them:** used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to two or more people or things previously mentioned or easily identified.
 
• The sentence tells about **books** which is plural. So 'them' should be the correct word that must fit the blank as it refers to the 'books' previously mentioned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *The assistant in the library picked up the books from the tables and put **them**__ back on the shelves.*
